track.title: Abuata (Tasnif-e Chehre Be Chehre)
track.notes: Includes the tasnif Chehre be Chehre (may have voice).

just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on Bk4 and dwells most on D in Phrase 1. Phrase 2 (0:06.1) introduces C, centred on Bk. Phrase 4 (0:37.6) introduces A, Cs, E, F, Gk, centred on C. The line peaks at Bk5 (905.5 Hz) at 0:15.7. It closes on Ck5, not the tonic (D5 → Ck5 → Bk4 → C5 → D5 → Ck5).

theory_fit.name: Farhat interval classes

flags: tonic A set in the catalog (pattern: Shur on A, same tuning as Saba's Abuata; Abu-Ata uses Shur's finalis (Farhat 1990, p. 35). The vote picked the 5th (E). Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 1232.4 Hz (D)
no inventory pitch at the tonic, but p01 (A) is +11 ¢ from it: probably the tonic itself, misplaced by bin quantisation of the tonic Hz
